I did my own investigation because I obviously don't trust them.

What I found is that the external dependency of the firmware with the critical vulnerability hidden in it was written by CoinKite's CTO 
@DocHex
 pretending to be someone else.

All of the following can be verified:

posts.author: oomahq
posts.name: Extractive Ghost of Unhosted Marcellus
posts.text:
As a SeedSigner user I'm very familiar with 
@nvk
's FUD of it.

One of his main talking points is that the SeedSigner and its dependencies cannot be verified down to the metal, whereas ColdCard's software stack is developed in-house at Coinkite, top-to-bottom and controlled.

posts.author: oomahq
posts.name: Extractive Ghost of Unhosted Marcellus
posts.text:
So imagine my surprise when it turns out that the CC's firmware depends on a random project maintained by a nym named 
@switck
, who joined GitHub on August 2020.

3 months later Coinkite's CTO was asking him for permission to use it in CC's firmware.
